scope: Generated empty-registry dispatch guard, method addition/removal/replacement, direct dispatch stores and a single encapsulated setter, with the actual CCL NO-APPLICABLE-METHOD-EXISTS condition and CONTINUE protocol.
implementation: Portable Lisp source is compiled through the accepted front end and an isolated backend extension. A stable closure owns a registry of method identities and direct/encapsulated dispatch cells. Removal filters by method identity; addition replaces an equal admitted specializer; recomputation selects a direct universal method, a table selector, or the missing-method entry. The callable checks emptiness even after a subsequent stale raw store. Table selection keeps T as fallback while searching EQL keys. No JS callback selects a method or delivers a condition.
condition: The bounded owner registry accepts twelve legacy rows or those rows plus the thirteenth NO-APPLICABLE-METHOD-EXISTS class. Its D1 instance, wrapper, GF and ARGS slots are derived from native CCL. A rooted two-argument constructor works in ordinary and owner-retry emitter modes. The missing-method entry exposes CONTINUE, which retries the same callable after a handler changes its registry. Specific handlers, resignalling, cleanup and decline use the existing Lisp condition path.
oracle: An independent native session uses ENSURE/DEFGENERIC, DEFMETHOD, REMOVE-METHOD and ADVISE. Both direct and advised empty calls reproduce U1's removed-method values. The required result is separately obtained by invoking CCL's NO-APPLICABLE-METHOD protocol, as the adopted LL11-b assertion requires, never relabelled as the defective native dispatch result. Reverse insertion, replacement, cleanup, resignalling and arity have native witnesses. Each native compilation exports the real condition class slots.
exclusions: This initial dispatch representation is a generated closure with a cons-based owner record, not a native funcallable-standard-instance or the full CLOS MOP. The covered standard-primary subset has one required argument, universal T and EQL specializers on fixnums or stable EQ identities. Other class precedence, multiple dispatch, qualifiers, custom method combinations and CALL-NEXT-METHOD are not admitted by this service.

One encapsulation layer is represented by a generated forwarding callable and its separately updated inner dispatch cell. Native advice supplies the independent protocol witness. General advice installation and nested encapsulations remain outside this unit.

Method records and state are trusted, well-formed owner data. There is no concurrent registry mutation, method enumeration bound or class-redefinition claim. The empty guard is independent of the prior dispatch selection; the tests cover direct and table selections in both modes.

No collection occurs during this dispatch corpus. Existing condition handling is replayed with twelve classes; the new constructor's two operands are rooted across an enabled allocation retry, but collector-triggered generic dispatch is not newly qualified here.

An unhandled or declined error ends at the accepted checked boundary with code 15; this is not a browser debugger implementation. A twelve-row owner cannot construct the new class and refuses; production owners using this service must provide all thirteen rows.

The compiler proposal and portable runtime source stay isolated pending review and acceptance. Native R6/R6a is newly executed for this exact compiler. No full CLOS completeness or performance claim is made.
